alternative: The opening format is the covariate. A plain sample that does not open deliberatively is an answer-first reply: short, with no derivation. Replies like that are wrong at a high rate that depends on the format, whatever the checkpoint. The untrained base shows the size of this effect. On MATH-500 problems where its plain T3 answer did not open deliberatively, the cued answer (T1) beat it by 0.516 per problem (null of result-1f98b0 / F51: T3 - T1 = -0.516 [-0.564, -0.467]). Step 100 adds about +0.03 to the cue's right rate (426.0 vs 410.5 of 500, result-6832a8). So cue-minus-answer-first-plain at step 100 should be about the base's format gap. That puts it near 0.45-0.55, inside [0.15, 0.75], and no account of what RL changed is needed: only the fact that answer-first text skips the derivation.
computation: 1) Find the consequence's 70 qualifying problems from the openings only, without reading any grade. Use the 4 step-100 plain samples (sample 0 from studies/rlneurons/results/ckptcue/s0100_plain-01, samples 1-3 from studies/rlneurons/results/ckptcue/s0100_plain_s123-01), apply the result-1f98b0 flag rule to the first 240 characters, and keep problems with >= 1 unflagged sample. 2) Open studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t3_items-01/per_problem.json. It holds base T3 (plain) and T1 (cue) right/wrong under v3, plus the first 240 characters of each answer. Apply the same flag rule to each T3 opening. 3) Take the problems that are among the 70 and whose base T3 answer is unflagged (answer-first). On them, g_base = mean(T1 right - T3 right). If fewer than 30 problems qualify, use all 500 problems with an unflagged T3 instead (that gives 0.516, the F51 null). 4) Get the cue shift from checkpoint to base, s = mean over the same problems of (step-100 cue right rate over the 4 samples in s0100_cue-01 + s0100_cue_s123-01) - (base T1 right). This uses cue arms only, never the plain grades the statistic tests. 5) Predicted D1 = g_base + s. If the 70-problem subset is too small, use s = 0.031 from the totals (426.0/500 - 410.5/500). Expected about 0.516 + 0.031 = 0.55; a harder subset pulls it toward 0.45.
